events.title: NBA: 2027 Champion

events.title: NBA: Steph Curry Next Team
events.description:
This market will resolve to the next team Steph Curry officially joins by February 11, 2027, 11:59 PM ET.

If Stephen Curry does not officially join a new team by February 11, 2027, 11:59 PM ET, this market will resolve to “Golden State Warriors”.

If Stephen Curry joins a team that is not listed, this market will resolve to “Other”.

If Stephen Curry is released, retires, or is not under contract with any professional team by February 11, 2027, 11:59 PM ET, this market will resolve to “Other”.

An official trade announcement prior to the market’s close date will immediately resolve this market to the corresponding option.

The primary resolution sources for this market will be official announcements from the Golden State Warriors and/or the acquiring team. A consensus of credible media reporting may also be used to resolve the market.

events.title: 2027 NBA Draft Lottery: 1st Pick
events.description:
This market will resolve based on which team holds the draft rights to the first overall pick at the conclusion of the 2027 NBA Draft Lottery.

If a listed team holds another franchise's draft pick via trade at the time of the lottery, and that traded pick results in the first overall selection, the holder of the draft rights is considered the winner.

If a traded pick is subject to protection (e.g., "top-5 protected"), the winner is determined by which team ultimately receives the first overall pick after all protections are applied.

A qualifying announcement will resolve this market to "Yes" regardless of when the team is scheduled to begin play, or whether the selection or approval is later reversed.

The primary resolution source will be official information from the NBA; however, a consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

events.title: Las Vegas NBA franchise and arena price?
events.description:
This market will resolve according to the combined price of the NBA's Las Vegas expansion franchise and a new arena for the team.

The combined price is the total for the franchise and a new arena under the selected ownership group's deal, as announced by the NBA or reported by a consensus of credible reporting. If the franchise price and the arena cost are reported separately, the two figures will be added together, but a combined figure for the franchise and the arena, when reported, will take precedence over that sum. An arena cost reported only as part of a larger real estate or development figure will be treated as not reported, and a combined figure that also covers such development will not qualify.

events.title: NBA: 2026-27 Points Per Game Leader
events.description:
This market will resolve in favor of the player that finishes the 2026-27 NBA regular season with the highest points per game average among qualified players. If the leader is not a listed player, the "Other" market will resolve to "Yes".

To qualify, a player must meet the NBA's minimum requirements for its official 2026-27 regular-season per-game leaderboard (a player who appears in at least 58 regular-season games qualifies), applied exactly as reflected on NBA.com/stats. Only 2026-27 NBA regular-season games count. NBA Cup group-play and knockout games other than the NBA Cup Championship game are regular-season games and count. Statistics from the preseason, the NBA Cup Championship game, the Play-In Tournament, the playoffs and the All-Star Game are excluded. If a player plays for more than one team during the season, his statistics from all teams are combined.

In the event of a tie for the highest points per game average, this market will resolve in favor of the tied player with more total points during the 2026-27 NBA regular season. If a tie still persists, each tied player's market will resolve to "No" and the "Other" market will resolve to "Yes".

If the 2026-27 NBA regular season concludes early, is shortened, or is truncated for any reason, the outcome shall be determined using available NBA statistics for completed games, with leaderboard qualification applied as the NBA applies it to the shortened season.

If the 2026-27 NBA regular season is cancelled, postponed after April 25, 2027, 11:59 PM ET, or it is unclear which player led the NBA in points per game within that timeframe, each listed player's market will resolve to "No" and the "Other" market will resolve to "Yes".

The resolution source for this market will be official information from the NBA, including NBA.com/stats; however, a consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

This market will resolve in favor of the player that finishes the 2026-27 NBA regular season with the highest rebounds per game average among qualified players. If the leader is not a listed player, the "Other" market will resolve to "Yes".

To qualify, a player must meet the NBA's minimum requirements for its official 2026-27 regular-season per-game leaderboard (a player who appears in at least 58 regular-season games qualifies), applied exactly as reflected on NBA.com/stats. Only 2026-27 NBA regular-season games count. NBA Cup group-play and knockout games other than the NBA Cup Championship game are regular-season games and count. Statistics from the preseason, the NBA Cup Championship game, the Play-In Tournament, the playoffs and the All-Star Game are excluded. If a player plays for more than one team during the season, his statistics from all teams are combined.

In the event of a tie for the highest rebounds per game average, this market will resolve in favor of the tied player with more total rebounds during the 2026-27 NBA regular season. If a tie still persists, each tied player's market will resolve to "No" and the "Other" market will resolve to "Yes".

If the 2026-27 NBA regular season concludes early, is shortened, or is truncated for any reason, the outcome shall be determined using available NBA statistics for completed games, with leaderboard qualification applied as the NBA applies it to the shortened season.

If the 2026-27 NBA regular season is cancelled, postponed after April 25, 2027, 11:59 PM ET, or it is unclear which player led the NBA in rebounds per game within that timeframe, each listed player's market will resolve to "No" and the "Other" market will resolve to "Yes".

The resolution source for this market will be official information from the NBA, including NBA.com/stats; however, a consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

events.title: NBA: 2026-27 Player Efficiency Rating (PER) Leader
events.description:
This market will resolve in favor of the player that finishes the 2026-27 NBA regular season with the highest Player Efficiency Rating (PER) among qualified players. If the leader is not a listed player, the "Other" market will resolve to "Yes".

Player Efficiency Rating (PER) is the per-minute productivity rating developed by John Hollinger, as calculated and published for the 2026-27 NBA regular season by Basketball-Reference.com. To qualify, a player must appear in at least 58 regular-season games. Only 2026-27 NBA regular-season games count. NBA Cup group-play and knockout games other than the NBA Cup Championship game are regular-season games and count. Statistics from the preseason, the NBA Cup Championship game, the Play-In Tournament, the playoffs and the All-Star Game are excluded. If a player plays for more than one team during the season, his statistics from all teams are combined.

In the event of a tie for the highest PER (to one decimal place as published), this market will resolve in favor of the tied player with more Win Shares during the 2026-27 NBA regular season, as published by Basketball-Reference.com. If a tie still persists, each tied player's market will resolve to "No" and the "Other" market will resolve to "Yes".

If the 2026-27 NBA regular season concludes early, is shortened, or is truncated for any reason, the outcome shall be determined using available statistics for completed games, with the games-played requirement reduced to 70 percent of the games each player's team completed, rounded up.

If the 2026-27 NBA regular season is cancelled, postponed after April 25, 2027, 11:59 PM ET, or it is unclear which qualified player led the NBA in PER within that timeframe, each listed player's market will resolve to "No" and the "Other" market will resolve to "Yes".

The resolution source for this market will be Basketball-Reference.com (https://www.basketball-reference.com/); however, if Basketball-Reference.com is unavailable, a consensus of credible statistical sources that publish PER by the same formula, such as ESPN, may be used.

Player Efficiency Rating (PER) is the per-minute productivity rating developed by John Hollinger, as calculated and published for the 2026-27 NBA regular season by Basketball-Reference.com. To qualify, a player must appear in at least 58 regular-season games. Only 2026-27 NBA regular-season games count. NBA Cup group-play and knockout games other than the NBA Cup Championship game are regular-season games and count. Statistics from the preseason, the NBA Cup Championship game, the Play-In Tournament, the playoffs and the All-Star Game are excluded. If a player plays for more than one team during the season, his statistics from all teams are combined.

In the event of a tie for the highest PER (to one decimal place as published), this market will resolve in favor of the tied player with more Win Shares during the 2026-27 NBA regular season, as published by Basketball-Reference.com. If a tie still persists, each tied player's market will resolve to "No" and the "Other" market will resolve to "Yes".

If the 2026-27 NBA regular season concludes early, is shortened, or is truncated for any reason, the outcome shall be determined using available statistics for completed games, with the games-played requirement reduced to 70 percent of the games each player's team completed, rounded up.

If the 2026-27 NBA regular season is cancelled, postponed after April 25, 2027, 11:59 PM ET, or it is unclear which qualified player led the NBA in PER within that timeframe, each listed player's market will resolve to "No" and the "Other" market will resolve to "Yes".

The resolution source for this market will be Basketball-Reference.com (https://www.basketball-reference.com/); however, if Basketball-Reference.com is unavailable, a consensus of credible statistical sources that publish PER by the same formula, such as ESPN, may be used.

events.title: NBA: 2026-27 Worst Regular Season Record
events.description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" for the team that finishes the 2026-27 NBA regular season with the worst record in the league. For the purpose of this market, the worst record in the league means the lowest winning percentage (wins divided by games played) in the final official NBA standings. Each other listed team's market will resolve to "No". If that team is not a listed team, the "Other" market will resolve to "Yes".

The 2026-27 NBA regular season is scheduled to run from October 20, 2026 to April 11, 2027. If at any point it becomes impossible for a listed team to finish the 2026-27 NBA regular season with the worst record in the league, the corresponding market will resolve to "No".

If two or more teams finish with the same winning percentage, this market will resolve in favor of the tied team ranked lowest in the final official NBA league-wide standings after the NBA's tiebreaker procedures are applied. If the NBA does not publish an ordering of the tied teams, each tied team's market will resolve to "No" and the "Other" market will resolve to "Yes".

If the 2026-27 NBA regular season is shortened, this market will resolve according to the final official standings of the shortened season. If the 2026-27 NBA regular season is cancelled, or has not concluded by April 25, 2027, 11:59 PM ET, each listed team's market will resolve to "No" and the "Other" market will resolve to "Yes".

The resolution source for this market will be official information from the NBA; however, a consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

events.title: NBA: LeBron James 2026-27 Regular Season Triple-Doubles
events.description:
Each market in this event names a number of triple-doubles. A market will resolve to "Yes" if LeBron James records at least its listed number of triple-doubles during the 2026-27 NBA regular season, and otherwise to "No".

A triple-double is a game in which a player records 10 or more in three of the five statistical categories of points, rebounds, assists, steals and blocks, per the official NBA box score, including any statistical corrections the NBA subsequently issues. Only 2026-27 NBA regular-season games count. NBA Cup group-play and knockout games other than the NBA Cup Championship game are regular-season games and count. Statistics from the preseason, the NBA Cup Championship game, the Play-In Tournament, the playoffs and the All-Star Game are excluded. If a player plays for more than one team during the season, his statistics from all teams are combined.

If LeBron James does not play in the 2026-27 NBA regular season, including because of injury or retirement, this market will resolve according to the number of triple-doubles he recorded, which may be zero.

If the 2026-27 NBA regular season is cancelled, shortened, or postponed after April 25, 2027, 11:59 PM ET, this market will resolve according to the number of triple-doubles LeBron James recorded in regular-season games completed by that time.

The resolution source for this market will be official information from the NBA, including NBA.com/stats; however, a consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

This market will resolve to "Yes" if LeBron James records 8 or more triple-doubles during the 2026-27 NBA regular season. Otherwise, it will resolve to "No".

A triple-double is a game in which a player records 10 or more in three of the five statistical categories of points, rebounds, assists, steals and blocks, per the official NBA box score, including any statistical corrections the NBA subsequently issues. Only 2026-27 NBA regular-season games count. NBA Cup group-play and knockout games other than the NBA Cup Championship game are regular-season games and count. Statistics from the preseason, the NBA Cup Championship game, the Play-In Tournament, the playoffs and the All-Star Game are excluded. If a player plays for more than one team during the season, his statistics from all teams are combined.

If LeBron James does not play in the 2026-27 NBA regular season, including because of injury or retirement, this market will resolve according to the number of triple-doubles he recorded, which may be zero.

If the 2026-27 NBA regular season is cancelled, shortened, or postponed after April 25, 2027, 11:59 PM ET, this market will resolve according to the number of triple-doubles LeBron James recorded in regular-season games completed by that time.

The resolution source for this market will be official information from the NBA, including NBA.com/stats; however, a consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

events.title: NBA: Players to Average 30+ PPG in 2026-27
events.description:

If a player plays for more than one team during the season, his statistics from all teams are combined.

If the 2026-27 NBA regular season concludes early, is shortened, or is truncated for any reason, this market will resolve using available NBA statistics for completed games, with leaderboard qualification applied as the NBA applies it to the shortened season.

If the 2026-27 NBA regular season is cancelled, or postponed after April 25, 2027, 11:59 PM ET, this market will resolve according to the player's average and qualification status in regular-season games completed by that time.

The resolution source for this market will be official information from the NBA, including NBA.com/stats; however, a consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

This market will resolve to "Yes" if Jayson Tatum averages 10.0 or more assists per game during the 2026-27 NBA regular season and meets the NBA's minimum requirement for its official regular-season per-game leaderboard (58 games played or 400 assists during the 2026-27 NBA regular season, as the NBA applies it). Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

The per-game average is the player's total regular-season assists divided by regular-season games played, as displayed to one decimal place on NBA.com/stats. Only 2026-27 NBA regular-season games count. NBA Cup group-play and knockout games other than the NBA Cup Championship game are regular-season games and count. Statistics from the preseason, the NBA Cup Championship game, the Play-In Tournament, the playoffs and the All-Star Game are excluded. If a player plays for more than one team during the season, his statistics from all teams are combined.

If the 2026-27 NBA regular season concludes early, is shortened, or is truncated for any reason, this market will resolve using available NBA statistics for completed games, with leaderboard qualification applied as the NBA applies it to the shortened season.

If the 2026-27 NBA regular season is cancelled, or postponed after April 25, 2027, 11:59 PM ET, this market will resolve according to the player's average and qualification status in regular-season games completed by that time.

The resolution source for this market will be official information from the NBA, including NBA.com/stats; however, a consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

events.title: NBA: Players to be Traded Before the 2027 Trade Deadline
events.description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if the listed player is traded to another NBA team between October 9, 2026 and the 2027 NBA trade deadline. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

For the purpose of this market, the 2027 NBA trade deadline is February 11, 2027, 3:00 PM ET, or any revised date and time the NBA officially announces, but no later than February 25, 2027, 11:59 PM ET. A trade counts once it has been officially processed and approved by the NBA. A trade that is later rescinded or voided for any reason after being officially processed will still count. A player who is waived, released, bought out, retires, or otherwise leaves his team by any means other than a trade will not count as traded.

The resolution source for this market will be official information from the NBA and the teams involved; however, a consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

events.title: Who will perform at the 2027 Big Game halftime show?
events.description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if the listed individual performs live and in person during the Super Bowl LXI halftime show currently scheduled for February 14, 2027. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No."

Qualifying performances include but are not limited to singing and dancing. An appearance during the event where an individual does not perform as an incorporated part of the show will not alone qualify for a "Yes" resolution.

"Dancing" is defined as deliberate, rhythmic body movement typically matched to music or a beat, such as swaying, stepping, or coordinated hand or body motions. Casual gesturing, clapping, or incidental body movement will not qualify. Dancing without the presence of music or a beat will qualify.

If this event is cancelled or otherwise delayed beyond March 31, 2027, 11:59 PM ET, this market will resolve to "No".

The primary resolution source for this market will be footage of the Super Bowl LXI halftime show, however a consensus of credible reporting will also be used.

This market will resolve to the tight end who finishes the 2026-27 NFL regular season (Weeks 1 through 18) as the highest-scoring tight end under standard PPR (points-per-reception) scoring per the default scoring of ESPN Fantasy Sports.

If two or more players are tied for the most total PPR fantasy points, this market will resolve in favor of the tied player that has a higher fantasy points per game average for the 2026 NFL regular season. If a tie still persists, this market will resolve in favor of the tied player whose last name comes first alphabetically.

If the 2026-27 NFL regular season is cancelled, postponed past January 26, 2027, 11:59 PM ET, or a leader cannot be determined within this timeframe, this market will resolve to "Other".

The resolution source will be official season-total statistics as reported by ESPN Fantasy Sports (https://www.espn.com/fantasy/).

This market will resolve to the FLEX-eligible player (a running back, wide receiver, or tight end) who finishes the 2026-27 NFL regular season (Weeks 1 through 18) as the highest-scoring FLEX-eligible player under standard PPR (points-per-reception) scoring per the default scoring of ESPN Fantasy Sports.

If two or more players are tied for the most total PPR fantasy points, this market will resolve in favor of the tied player that has a higher fantasy points per game average for the 2026 NFL regular season. If a tie still persists, this market will resolve in favor of the tied player whose last name comes first alphabetically.

If the 2026-27 NFL regular season is cancelled, postponed past January 26, 2027, 11:59 PM ET, or a leader cannot be determined within this timeframe, this market will resolve to "Other".

The resolution source will be official season-total statistics as reported by ESPN Fantasy Sports (https://www.espn.com/fantasy/).

This market will resolve to “Yes” if the listed player is announced as the cover athlete of Sony Interactive’s MLB The Show 27, or if the player is explicitly depicted on the cover. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

Only explicit depictions of the player or their likeness (including but not limited to: a player’s face, a clear depiction in uniform including logo and/or number) will be considered for this market’s resolution.

All editions (e.g. standard, deluxe, bundle) of the game for console platforms slated for release by March 31, 2027, 11:59 PM ET will count toward this market’s resolution.

If MLB The Show 27 does not release, or it cannot be determined if a listed player is included on the cover by April 15, 2026, 11:59 PM ET, this market will resolve to “No”.

The primary resolution source will be an official announcement from Sony Interactive and/or the player; however, a consensus of credible reporting may also be used.
